findings.title: Migration can crash when embed_category is unset or does not match a category
findings.body: The migration reads `execute(...)[0]['id']` without checking that the query returned a row. `embed_category` defaults to an empty string and commonly will not join to any category, so the result is empty and indexing `[0]` returns nil; the migration then raises on `['id']` and aborts the upgrade. The fallback query for `uncategorized_category_id` has the same risk if that setting row is absent. Use a nil-safe first-row lookup and fall back when no category exists.

findings.title: Old host values are interpolated raw into SQL and inserted without normalization
findings.body: The INSERT is built as `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` from the old `embeddable_hosts` setting. A value containing a single quote breaks the migration (and is an injection primitive), and values are inserted directly without going through `EmbeddableHost`'s scheme/path trimming. Existing settings that contain `http://example.com` or `https://example.com/path` will be stored in that raw form, but `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` queries `lower(host) = uri.host`, so those hosts can never match after the upgrade and embedding silently stops. Quote the value and normalize each host before insertion, preferably by creating records through the model.

findings.title: Blank host raises NoMethodError instead of adding a validation error
findings.body: The `before_validation` hook calls `self.host.sub!` unconditionally. If `embeddable_host[host]` is missing or nil, `host` is nil and the admin create/update request raises NoMethodError before validations run, returning a 500 instead of a validation response. Guard against a blank host or rely on a presence validation before string manipulation.

findings.title: Hosts with an explicit port can be saved but can never match a request
findings.body: The format validator accepts an optional `:port`, and the before_validation hook does not remove it, so a host such as `example.com:3000` can be stored. `record_for_host` uses `URI(host).host`, which drops the port, and then binds only `example.com` into `lower(host) = ?`; a stored port can therefore never match. Strip the port when saving or include it when matching.

findings.title: Host validation rejects valid TLDs longer than five characters
findings.body: The new format regex uses `[a-z]{2,5}` for the TLD. Valid hosts such as `example.museum`, `example.travel`, and many newer TLDs cannot be added, even though they are valid embeddable hosts and could be used with the old site setting. Allow longer TLDs or use a dedicated hostname validator.

findings.title: Updating or deleting a missing embeddable host returns a 500
findings.body: Both `update` and `destroy` fetch with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and immediately call `save_host(host)` or `host.destroy`. If the id is invalid or the record was deleted concurrently, `host` is nil and the request raises NoMethodError instead of returning a 404/error response. Use `find_by` with a nil check, or `find` with `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` handling.

findings.title: Saving a host without a chosen category overwrites category with undefined
findings.body: After a successful save, the component sets `host.category` from its local `categoryId`, not from the server-returned `category_id`. For a new host, or when the chooser is cleared, `categoryId` is null while the controller has assigned `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`; `Discourse.Category.findById(null)` returns undefined. The row then loses its category badge, and the next click on Edit throws when `edit()` reads `this.get('host.category.id')`. Update `categoryId`/`category` from the saved host response instead.

findings.title: Fruit-by-id fixture ignores the requested id
findings.body: The `/fruits/:id` handler always returns `fruits[0]`, whose id is 1, even though the updated store test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)`. The test therefore does not verify that `find` requests and hydrates the requested record and passes even though the handler returned the wrong fruit. Return the record matching `request.params.id` and assert the fetched id in the test.

findings.title: Category and embeddable-host fabricator files are swapped
findings.body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines only `:embeddable_host`, while all category fabricators including `:private_category` were moved into `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. The suite may still pass because Fabrication loads all fabricator files, but this makes file-based loading/tooling and future maintenance confusing; restore the original contents to the matching filenames.

findings.title: expandable_first_post test no longer tests the embeddable-host condition
findings.body: After `Topic#expandable_first_post?` stopped checking `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts`, this test still says 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' but only passes because `has_topic_embed?` is false. The inner block also fabricates a host that the method no longer consults. The test no longer covers the behavior described and can hide regressions around removing hosts; rename/restructure it or explicitly test the current `embed_truncate?`/`has_topic_embed?` conditions.
